newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says it can reverse science brain drain.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says it can reverse science brain drain.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party said on Tuesday that if it comes to office in the May 1 election it will implement a plan which could reverse a flow of British scientific talent overseas.
"Our scientists will want to come home. We will see the reversal of the brain drain and the beginnings of a brain gain," education and employment spokesman David Blunkett told a news conference.

The centrepiece of the strategy is the party's planned National Endowment for Science, Technology and the Arts (NESTA) which would work to protect the intellectual property rights of British inventors and give high-tech businesses start up grants.
Blunkett said NESTA would be funded initially from endowments from scientists and inventors from copyright and patents.
But after the winding up of the Millennium Commission, an unspecified proportion of the funds it receives from the National Lottery will be diverted to NESTA, he said.
Labour said testimonials for the policy it has collected from British scientists working abroad showed its "brain gain" claims were justified.

Michael Duff, a professor of theoretical physics at the Texas A and M University, told the news conference via video: "It...will help create the kind of environment that will once again make Britain the sort of place that UK scientists abroad will want to come home to."

But none of the scientists quoted by the party guaranteed that if Labour won on May 1, they would be buying one-way air tickets back to Britain for themselves and their families soon afterwards. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
